items.title: Frank Goudie Interview
items.q: Buck lay off 20 years and came back like... like a jack.

ctx.x: But they didn't lay off. And still they were shot. Yeah. Buck lay off 20 years and came back like... like a jack. Yeah. No teeth? No, uh... In just his hat. Yeah. They didn't have no trumpet back. But it shows in the... But I'm going to take a shave. Oh, yeah. And if you want to go and get some cigarette. See what's that?

Testing. A clip from Melody Maker. Uh, Frank, Big Boy, Goody and Danny Polo departed from this country before the swing craze hit its peak. The same departing. The same departing somewhat from the style in which they had been reared in America. If Bill Coleman showed continental Europeans how the jazz trumpet should and could and should be played. Dickie Wells at Trombone, Betty Carter at the alto sax, Coleman Hawkins at tenor sax, and Chittison at piano. Goody certainly revealed to them the mysteries of jazz…
